decisions.decision: Owner 2026-11-01: "Flashing animation before a punch that show the direction of the upcoming punch would be ideal" and "Don't re-use from puff, new for boxing game." The Boxer gets its own flashing direction warning; it does not reuse Grand Puff's warning or its code.

decisions.subject: Boxer hooks
decisions.question: Review decision 2: spread the punch paths, or add side hooks?
decisions.decision: Owner 2026-11-01: "Hooks should also be a part of the game, which adds variation and disrupts the simple Punch block." Hooks are part of the Boxer; the jab lanes are spread as well.

decisions.subject: Boxer Title Imp counter gate
decisions.question: Review decision 1: should Title Imp's counter open only after a block?
decisions.decision: Owner reply 2026-11-01, "Use the defaults", accepting the stated default: a block opens the star; after two unblocked punches in a row the imp tires and opens anyway, so she is never stuck.

decisions.subject: Boxer counter window
decisions.question: Review decision 3: counter window fixed or open-ended?
decisions.decision: Owner reply 2026-11-01, "Use the defaults", accepting the stated default: 2.4 s, never below 2.0 s; when help is on, it stays open until she punches.

decisions.subject: Boxer sound cues
decisions.question: Review decision 4: reuse existing sound effects or record new ones?
decisions.decision: Owner reply 2026-11-01, "Use the defaults", accepting the stated default: reuse existing sound effects for the launch, the "now" moment and the count-in ticks; no new voice recordings.

decisions.subject: Boxer engine work start
decisions.question: Review decision 5: when should Codex start?
decisions.decision: Owner reply 2026-11-01, "Use the defaults", accepting the stated default: after the 7 November demo; Codex builds on top of codex/boxer-contact-engine-20261031, which passes CI but is not merged into dev while dev is in its demo freeze.

decisions.subject: Boxer as a recurring engine
decisions.question: What should the Boxer become across the adventure?
decisions.decision: Owner 2026-11-01: the minigame will "reoccur a minimum of four to five times, with new additions", complexity grows with each, "We are building the engine that is allowing these next steps to come into place", and "Using this engine is a part of the final boss. Battle is likely." The owner asked to focus on the engine and gameplay additions rather than plot placement.

decisions.subject: Boxer edition order
decisions.question: Roadmap decision 1: is the edition order right (hooks, then rhythm, then reading the guard, then two at once)?
decisions.decision: Owner reply 2026-11-01, "Use the defaults", accepting the stated default: yes; each step needs the one before it.

decisions.subject: Boxer Family Sparring
decisions.question: Roadmap decision 2: include optional Family Sparring?
decisions.decision: Owner reply 2026-11-01, "Use the defaults", accepting the stated default: yes, in Edition 3, as a parent-started mode outside the required path.

decisions.subject: Boxer ducking and dodging
decisions.question: Roadmap decision 3: keep ducking and dodging out?
decisions.decision: Owner reply 2026-11-01, "Use the defaults", accepting the stated default: yes; revisit only if the gloves stop being enough.

decisions.subject: Boxer opponent representation
decisions.question: Roadmap decision 4: keep the opponent as floating gloves for now?
decisions.decision: Owner reply 2026-11-01, "Use the defaults", accepting the stated default: yes; a face or body behind the gloves can come later without changing the engine.

decisions.subject: One Roshan rig with data-only costume skins
decisions.question: Owner correction to the swimming costume test architecture
decisions.decision: These look good, but are obviously of the wrong design. These are individually building each costumed creation as a new character, as opposed to streamlining a good system to implement skins on the same skeletal frame. Identify this part of the rigging process and best workflow to be able to address it.

decisions.subject: Costume-to-skin conversion guide and master audit criteria
decisions.question: Owner extends the reusable skin workflow into an efficient conversion guide
decisions.decision: The workflow should go a step further, and be able to provide a guide (sent to the master audit, in addition to the criteria here also contributing to master audit) for costumes to be translated into the proper skin binding format for improved efficiency

decisions.subject: Whole-game soundtrack identity and reference design
decisions.question: Owner-initiated scope correction during soundtrack development
decisions.decision: Develop a whole-game multi-genre sonic identity, adding the original SNES Donkey Kong Country soundtrack as a concrete influence and realizing the feel through modern VST performances. Palette, instrument, theme and reference design is a key phase. Opera House, Sky Lagoon and Castle are improving studies but are not polished enough for release. Specific proposed palette choices still require review; the existing UVI-family, protected-media and release constraints retain their scopes.

decisions.subject: Performing ensemble and historical music references
decisions.question: Owner-initiated organization of the sonic mission as a band
decisions.decision: The overall sonic guide is a good mission statement. Organize the soundtrack as a logical group of musicians, each with a clear historical reference point to guide uncertain stylistic and technique decisions. The existing cast is a good start but is incomplete; add a DJ/electronic producer so that element can mix with the music. Detailed proposed personnel, programs and cue casts are not automatically accepted for release.

decisions.subject: Electronic producer genre range and console-era colors
decisions.question: Owner-initiated correction to the proposed single producer reference
decisions.decision: The DJ/producer needs several reference lanes because no one artist supplies the full genre range. Quantic’s suitability is uncertain. Include qualities from the KPop Demon Hunters soundtrack, bright dance music, Condard-like retro glitch-hop and selected Game Boy/NES/SNES-era colors. New proposed tracks, patches and library purchases are not automatically accepted by this direction.

decisions.subject: RetroPlug/LSDJ exception and Ember King chiptune theme
decisions.question: Owner-directed tool installation and explicit UVI-rule exception
decisions.decision: Install RetroPlug to use the already downloaded LSDJ for Game Boy tones. This is an explicit exception to the UVI-only instrument rule. Chiptune is the theme for the Ember King. Other instrumentation retains the existing UVI/Sunbird direction; tool/genre authorization does not establish a finished composition, runtime replacement or release acceptance.

decisions.subject: Multi-instrumentalist creative collective and current lo-fi rhythm language
decisions.question: Owner-initiated correction of fixed instrumental chairs
decisions.decision: Organize the band as multi-instrumentalist creatives working mostly within related instrument classes, with shifting roles based on what the song needs. The group explores context to compose a DKC-reminiscent soundtrack with advanced tools. Add a traditional percussionist; world drum kits are reported available in the current configuration. Lo-fi beats are an underlying theme for the current time, with a metal-style kit not the current rhythmic default. Detailed proposed capabilities, references and exact presets remain review choices.

decisions.subject: Detailed performer profiles and song construction
decisions.question: Owner-directed expansion of the creative collective into practical performer knowledge
decisions.decision: Create an individual master-audit log for every performer, detailing musical skills, knowledge, techniques, styles and performance attributes, and use those profiles in the construction of each song. Parallel profile-research chats were explicitly requested. Profile content and exact musical realizations remain reviewable design work; no new composition or release acceptance is implied.

decisions.subject: Bonobo as the producer identity
decisions.question: Owner-selected single artistic identity for the producer
decisions.decision: Bonobo is the ideal single primary artistic identity for the producer. Continue profile and soundtrack design around this coherent centre; earlier pop, bright dance, retro glitch-hop and console/chip capabilities remain contextual requirements rather than equal competing producer identities. This resolves the earlier uncertainty about Quantic or a single primary reference and grants no composition or release acceptance.

decisions.subject: Percussion Factory added to the instrument resources
decisions.question: Owner report of newly added soundbank
decisions.decision: Percussion Factory has been added and should be considered a meaningful soundbank resource for the project. Exact installed edition, programs, mapping and performance behavior still require native verification before claiming audition or production readiness.

decisions.subject: Expanded soundbank palette and three private soundtrack tests
decisions.question: Owner continuation after demonstrating additional indexed soundbanks
decisions.decision: Confirm the added libraries as part of the available package, determine arrangements for Opera House, Sky Lagoon and Castle, then produce test tracks with the new profiled Falcon/REAPER Lua workflow. This separately authorizes private test construction while final arrangement review remains pending; it does not accept unheard music or direct runtime replacement/release.

decisions.subject: Whole DKC soundtrack study and original instrumentation priority
decisions.question: How should soundtrack instrumentation be researched and reconciled with the existing musician collective?
decisions.decision: Build a separate entire-soundtrack DKC profile: locate original YouTube recordings and MIDI backings first, then map all audible instruments to available files and stress-test their closeness. In-game instrumentation always wins a conflict with the musician roster; the roster must never restrict the study. Record missing sources, instruments and articulations in the master audit. This research commission does not accept any unheard match or authorize runtime replacement.

decisions.subject: Rational revisable DKC interpretation
decisions.question: Should ambiguity leave DKC study areas undecided?
decisions.decision: Interpret the work rather than merely document it. Where evidence is ambiguous, form a rational supported opinion that can be revised later, and proceed rather than leaving missing areas because information is incomplete. Search comprehensively for MIDI logs and stress-test them against interpretations of the original YouTube clips. This directs working musical decisions, not invented historical facts or automatic performance/release acceptance.

decisions.subject: Two-layer DKC soundtrack revision and lively performance direction
decisions.question: How should the DKC profile become a revision guide?
decisions.decision: Provide a detailed complete outline of every melody by theme, instruments and tone, followed by application of the master-audit cast. Develop a livelier interpretation with mild artistic liberties, selective swing and intentional irregularity rather than perfectly quantized performance; research Cuban/Afropop influences and integrate specific performance notes. This commission advances the written guide; original in-game instrument authority remains primary and rendered acceptance is separate.

decisions.subject: Continue normal green integration into dev during demo preparation
decisions.question: Does demo preparation freeze dev or stop otherwise authorized updates?
decisions.decision: Owner, 2026-11-03: "I'm told dev is frozen, why? We should still be pushing updates to dev!" Continue merging and pushing completed, probes-green authorized work into dev through the established task-branch integration workflow. Supersedes ODR-DEMO-FREEZE-20261031 where it limits dev to DR0-DR7, parks otherwise authorized tasks, or holds dev at a release candidate. Demo priorities, other scoped owner answers, security, protected assets, budgets, save/device/child/owner acceptance and dev-to-master release gates retain their scopes. This is no new feature commission or release instruction.

decisions.subject: Six-track iterative DKC soundtrack production
decisions.question: Is actual source-led and expressive soundtrack production commissioned?
decisions.decision: Revise the four existing DKC studies and make two additional tracks. First compare instrument selection and tonality against the reference documents and originals, then develop live-instrument-style performances iteratively toward subjectively high quality, with an estimated 10–25 revisions as useful. Retain and assess valuable alternate inspirations/takes and finish with the critical artistic decisions as guidance for the remaining production. This directly authorizes these private arrangements; final owner/runtime acceptance is separate.

decisions.subject: Layered production and mastering with repeated comprehensive audits
decisions.question: What follows the initial six-track construction?
decisions.decision: Master the previous tracks with attention to properly layered production, clarity, soundstage and overall polish. Perform between five and ten comprehensive evaluation audits before approval. This commissions the mastering phase; it does not grant musical acceptance to unseen results.
